hazard.hybrid: The word isn't in SB 53; the two catastrophic-risk definitions at ranks 1-2 are the right nearest material. Ranks 3-20 are filler, and nothing in hybrid's output says the term is absent.
hazard.outline: Correctly flagged 'nothing in scope seems to answer this'. That's the most useful thing either tool says for this query.

catastrophic risk.hybrid: Both definitions are at the top, marked as defining the term (good). The test case is missed, though: the equity exclusions §22757.16 (#46) and §1107.2 (#65) don't contain the words 'catastrophic risk' and are absent from the top 20, so a reader gets an incomplete definition. 'Property' (#28) is also missing. Four digest passages (ranks 11, 14, 19, 20) take room that operative uses of the term (#12 finding j, #66 preemption) should have.
catastrophic risk.outline: Good: both equity sections were opened (L215, L303), as were both definitions, flagged 'defines'. Opening the digest (L36-44, L50-54) is noise for a definitional question.

loss of control.hybrid: Ranks 1-3 are right. The noise comes from single words matching on their own: 'loss' pulls in both equity sections ('loss of value of equity', ranks 6-7), and 'control' pulls in the affiliate definition ('controlling, controlled by', rank 8). The anchors mislead too. #19 is anchored on the '$1B … loss of property' sentence, not on (C) 'Evading the control', and #55 on the weight-theft item, not on item (3). A reader following the anchor reads the wrong line. Framework item (10), 'circumventing oversight mechanisms' (#30), is only at rank 14.
loss of control.outline: It covered the right places, but in wide ranges (L93-112, L257-270). It also spent room on equity, severability and SEC. 6.

humans can no longer shut down or correc.hybrid: Poor. Rank 1 is OES revoking a regulation, which matches only 'revoke'/'correct'-like wording. The catastrophic-risk definition holding (C) evading control is at rank 15, anchored on (B), and the incident definition with 'Loss of control' (#20) is missing. The vote line (rank 10) and the digest preamble also appear. The paraphrase shares no words with SB 53's phrasing, and the semantic side didn't bridge the gap.
humans can no longer shut down or correc.outline: Flagged 'nothing in scope seems to answer this'. That's half right: SB 53 has no shutdown language, but (C) and incident (3) are its answer, and the flag might make an agent stop looking. The opened ranges (front matter L26-28, L56-60, CalCompute L220-238) are mostly noise. L94-105 does cover (C).

misalignment.hybrid: The term is absent from SB 53. Its one misalignment provision, the deception incident (#20, item 4), is at rank 3, anchored on the definition's opening line. The equity section is at rank 2, which is noise. Site chrome (L14) is at rank 20.
misalignment.outline: The 'nothing in scope' flag is fair for the word, but the deception incident is a real answer. The opened ranges include L14 site navigation, L26-28 and L219 (CalCompute headers), which is noise.

whistleblower.hybrid: Every passage of the Labor Code chapter is in the top 20, which is good. But the digest's summaries are at ranks 1 and 3, above the operative prohibition (#59, rank 5), and the 'covered employee' definition, which decides who is protected, is only at rank 13. The AG's annual whistleblower report (#44, L210-212) is missing; it sits in §22757.14, under a heading about the Department of Technology.
whistleblower.outline: It opened the whole chapter, which is right. It also opened L14 site chrome, L20 'SHARE THIS', and CalCompute's membership (L239-248), all noise.

serious incident.hybrid: SB 53's term is 'critical safety incident', and the passages for it rank well (ranks 1, 4, 5). The definition (#20) should come first. Ranks 2-3 are the catastrophic-risk definitions, pulled in by 'serious injury'. That's a different concept, and an agent could conflate the two.
serious incident.outline: It opened the right places, and the whole reporting section (L166-198) as one range. That's correct but wide.

what must a developer publish or report.hybrid: Rank 1 is right (the transparency report). Rank 2, incident reporting, isn't a pre-deployment duty. The definition of 'deploy' (#21), which decides whether evaluator access triggers the report, is only at rank 15. Rank 8 (L206, 'before beginning to train or deploy', about the Department of Technology's review) is a lexical false friend.
what must a developer publish or report.outline: Good: L127-165 covers the framework, both transparency-report tiers, redaction and false statements, and L98-112 covers 'deploy'. The CalCompute and whistleblower ranges are noise.

evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.hybrid: SB 53 holds no evidence, and neither tool says so. Rank 1 (#30) is right as a passage, but its anchor is item (6) 'substantially modified', not item (10) 'circumventing oversight'. The deception incident (#20) is at rank 10. 'Evidence' matched the burden-of-proof clause (rank 7) and the Department of Technology's 'assess recent evidence' (rank 12), both lexical noise.
evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.outline: Not flagged as unanswerable, though the document can't answer an evidence question. Topical relevance passed for answerability.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.hybrid: Poor. The only place SB 53 treats cyber as a model capability, (B) autonomous cyberattack (#19), is at rank 13, anchored on its opening line, and the Labor Code's (B) (#53) is missing. Rank 1 is finding (m), on capabilities emerging. 'cyber' seems not to match 'cyberattack' or 'cybersecurity' (compound words), so the lexical side found nothing and the ranking is generic 'frontier model capability' material.
cyber capabilities of frontier models.outline: L94-112 covers (B), and L127-165 covers the weight-security item. The rest is wide and generic.

how the severity or acceptability of a r.hybrid: The catastrophic-risk definition (rank 2) is right. The framework passage where the developer sets its own thresholds and adequacy (#29) is at rank 11, and the equity exclusion (#46) is missing. The 24-hour clause (rank 14) and preemption (rank 7) are noise.
how the severity or acceptability of a r.outline: Reasonable coverage, but it didn't open L215 (equity). Opening L290-302 (injunction procedure) is noise.

what is SB 53's definition of catastroph.hybrid: This is the test case, and it fails. Rank 1 is the Department of Technology's 'management of catastrophic risk' (#43). The actual definitions are at ranks 5-6 and aren't flagged as defining, though the bare-term query flagged them. The equity exclusion (#46) and 'property' (#28) are missing. One confound: the query names 'SB 53', which may pull toward passages that contain 'SB 53' (the digest heading). That isn't what put #43 first, though.
what is SB 53's definition of catastroph.outline: It opened L303 (Labor Code equity) but not L215 (TFAIA equity), so the main definition's modifier is unread. It didn't mark 'defines' for this phrasing.

does SB 53 require developers to comply.hybrid: Rank 1 is the digest heading 'SB 53, Wiener.', apparently because the query contains 'SB 53'. Rank 2 is federal equivalence, matched on 'comply'. The operative answer, 'write, implement, comply with' (#29), is only at rank 8, just above the digest sentence that leaves the verb out (rank 9). The penalty for failing to comply (#45) is at rank 5, which is good. A reader of the top 3 would learn nothing true.
does SB 53 require developers to comply.outline: L127-165 begins with the answer line, and L213-214 is opened, which is good. But the first opened range, L32-60, is the whole digest, including the misleading sentence.

who can be penalised under SB 53, and by.hybrid: The answer, §22757.15 (#45), is at rank 9, below the digest heading (rank 1, the 'SB 53' match), severability (rank 2) and whistleblower notice (rank 3). The 'large frontier developer' definition (#26), which bounds who is penalised, is missing.
who can be penalised under SB 53, and by.outline: L213-214 is opened. The 22 opened ranges spread across the whole document, so the answer isn't distinguished from the rest.

is theft of model weights a critical saf.hybrid: Good: both incident definitions are at ranks 2-3, and the framework's weight-security item (#30) is at rank 7. Better would be the definitions first, then 'model weight' (#27, rank 16). The reporting duty at rank 1 is acceptable context.

does SB 53 require independent third-par.hybrid: Rank 1 is the digest heading again (the 'SB 53' match). The answer passages are at ranks 2-3 (good). 'Independent' matched the burden-of-proof clause's 'legitimate, independent reasons' (rank 14), and 'evaluation' matched CalCompute's report contents (rank 7). Both are lexical noise.
does SB 53 require independent third-par.outline: L127-137 and L140-165 hold the answer. The digest (L32-60) and CalCompute ranges are noise. L266-270 (the deception incident's 'outside of the context of an evaluation') is a lexical false friend.

how does SB 53 treat internal use of fro.hybrid: Mostly good: the OES confidential channel (rank 1), framework item (10) (rank 2, anchored on item 6), and the transmittal duty (#33, rank 3) are all near the top. 'Internal' also matched the whistleblower 'internal process' (ranks 7 and 16), a lexical false friend. #37 (Public Records Act exemption for internal-use reports) is missing.
how does SB 53 treat internal use of fro.outline: Good coverage. It also opened the whistleblower internal process and injunction ranges, which are noise from the same word.
